references.text: God creates man in His image, which is the direct justification given in Gen 9:6 for why shedding blood is forbidden.
The Lord tells Cain that Abel's blood cries out from the ground, reflecting the value of blood and the consequences of shedding innocent blood.
Whoever strikes a human being dead shall die. This is a legal formulation of the principle of bloodshed from Gen 9:6.
Blood defiles the land, and it can only be atoned for by the blood of the murderer – a direct parallel to the principle that whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed.
David asks to be delivered from bloodguilt, which shows the seriousness of bloodshed and God's abhorrence of murder.
Proverbs lists things the Lord hates, including hands that shed innocent blood, emphasizing the value of human life.
Jesus says that all who take up the sword shall perish by the sword – a New Testament parallel to the principle in Gen 9:6.
James points out that man is created in God's image, which directly reflects the justification for the prohibition against bloodshed in Gen 9:6.
Genesis 1:27 provides the theological basis for the judgment in 9:6 by defining humanity's inherent value as God's image.
Ezekiel confirms the principle in 9:6 that righteous judges must judge those who shed blood.
Ezekiel applies the principle of retribution from 9:6 as a judgment against nations.
Revelation affirms the principle of 9:6 that those who shed blood deserve to have their own blood shed.
Leviticus 24:21 is a direct legal restatement of the life-for-life principle in 9:6.
Leviticus 17:11 explains the theology behind 9:6: blood is life, therefore life is required for life.
Genesis 5:1 confirms the creation basis for the judgment in 9:6.
Psalm 58:12 confirms the theological basis of 9:6: God judges on earth.
